newsitem.title: USA: Glickman, Fischler have "productive" talk on row.
newsitem.headline: Glickman, Fischler have "productive" talk on row.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Dan Glickman and EU Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler had a "productive conversation" earlier Tuesday about the current trans-Atlantic dispute over meat import regulations, a USDA spokesman said.
"They had a good productive conversation," said Jim Petterson.

Petterson could not give any details of the conversation, but said the Agriculture Department will make an announcement Wednesday on whether or not the dispute has been settled and any subsequent action.

Glickman told a group of farm broadcasters early Tuesday morning that he would be calling Fischler later in the day in hopes of reaching an agreement on meat imports and averting a major trade disruption this week.

The United States has said it would remove more than 100 European meat and poultry packing plants from its list of approved exporters if a deal is not reached by April 30. The move would halt some $300 million worth of European meat shipments to the United States, mostly Danish pork products.

Poultry issues have proved to be the major obstacle towards reaching an agreement, and U.S. meat and poultry officials said Tuesday they were not optimistic a deal could be worked out regarding poultry.

Industry officials said an agreement on everything but poultry could be likely be reached, which -- while not a completely satisfactory agreement -- would at least avert a damaging escalation of the fight.
